editorial:
Imagine meeting a sweet old man who spends his days caring for his grandkids and helping neighbors. That is exactly how the world sees Albert Fish in the 1920s. He seems like a saint, but behind that kind smile is one of the worst monsters in history. You will feel a chill down your spine as the movie peels back the layers of his double life. It is not a fun ride, but it is a gripping look at how a predator can hide in plain sight while everyone around him thinks he is a good person.

The acting is the strongest part here because it makes the character feel terrifyingly real. While the plot moves a bit slowly in some spots, the tension keeps you glued to the screen. If you love true crime stories that make you think, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a high-quality digital rental on Apple TV to get the best picture. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this dark piece of history on your shelf.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the law finally catching up to Albert Fish. After a long search, police find him and bring him to trial for his horrible crimes. He does not show any regret and even talks about his dark urges during the trial. Eventually, the court finds him guilty and sentences him to death. The film wraps up with him being executed in the electric chair, ending his reign of terror once and for all.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime and psychological thrillers.
